questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of the State Public Service Commission?

options.text: It conducts examinations for appointments to the services of the state.
It is consulted in all disciplinary matters affecting a person serving under the government of the state in a civil capacity.
It is consulted on any claim for the award of a pension in respect of injuries sustained by a person while serving under the government of the state.
It is consulted while making reservations of appointments or posts in favour of any backward class of citizens.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **State Public Service Commissions (PSCs)** are government agencies responsible for the recruitment and selection of candidates for various civil service jobs within the state.
 
• Their main function is** to ensure that the recruitment and selection process is fair, transparent, and based on merit.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• Some of the specific functions of the **State Public Service Commission** include:

 
 
• **Recruitment of candidates**: The PSCs are responsible for conducting examinations and interviews to recruit candidates for various positions in the state government. These positions can include administrative, judicial, police, and other public service jobs.
 
• **Conducting examinations**: The PSCs are responsible for conducting competitive examinations to select eligible candidates for various posts in the state government. These exams can be conducted for various levels, such as Class I, II, III, and IV.
 
• **Setting eligibility criteria:** The PSCs set eligibility criteria for various posts based on educational qualifications, age, experience, and other relevant factors.
 
• **Advising the government: **The PSCs advise the government on matters related to recruitment, selection, and promotion of civil servants.
 
• Promoting fairness and transparency: The PSCs ensure that the recruitment process is conducted fairly and transparently, without any discrimination or favoritism.
 
• **Reducing corruption:** The PSCs play an important role in reducing corruption in the recruitment and selection process by ensuring that it is based on merit and not on any other factors.
 
 
 
• In summary, the State Public Service Commission plays a crucial role in ensuring that the state government has a qualified and competent workforce. They ensure that the recruitment process is fair, transparent, and based on merit, thereby promoting good governance and reducing corruption.

questions.question: In September 2022, who has been appointed as the new Attorney General of India?

The correct answer is __**R. Venkataramani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The current Attorney General of India **is **R. Venkataramani**.
 
• As the 16th Attorney General, he took over the position on October 1, 2022.
 
• Venugopal K. K. was his predecessor. In2010, the Law Commission of India designated him as a member.
 
• In addition to serving as acting Special Senior Counsel for the State of Andhra Pradesh, he has appeared on behalf of the State of Tamil Nadu for the previous twelve years.
 
• Ram Jethmalani: He was a renowned lawyer and politician who passed away in 2019.
 
• Kailash Vasdev: There is no information available on any person with this name being appointed as the Attorney General of India.
 
• Jagdeep Dhankhar: He is the current Governor of West Bengal and has not been appointed as the Attorney General of India.

• The Indian government's primary legal advisor is the Attorney General of India.
 
• **Under Article 76(1)** of the Constitution, the President of India appoints the Attorney General, who serves for the President's pleasure.
 
• The appointment is made at the Union Cabinet's request. To be appointed as a Supreme Court judge, the Attorney General must fulfill the requirements.
 
• Thus, the Attorney General ought to have spent at least five years as a judge or ten years as an advocate in a high court.

questions.question: The 15th Finance Commission has been constituted by the President of India for a period of ______ years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The 15th Finance commission **was established to make recommendations for a** five-year period beginning on April 1, 2020**.
 
• The commission's major goals were to **"strengthen cooperative federalism, increase the quality of government spending, and contribute to fiscal stability."**
 
• The Government of India established the Fifteenth Finance Commission in November 2017 after receiving assent from the President of India through a notification in the Indian Gazette.
 
• The commission's chairman is **Nand Kishore Singh**, and its full-time members are** Shaktikanta Das **and **Anoop Singh**, with part-time members Ramesh Chand and Ashok Lahiri.
 
• Shaktikanta Das, who resigned from the commission to become the governor of the Reserve Bank of India, was replaced by **Ajay Narayan Jha**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__

 
• **The Finance Commissions** are commissions appointed by the President of India on a regular basis under **Article 280 of the Indian Constitution** to define the financial connections between the central government and state governments.
 
• The** Finance Commission Act of 1951** constituted the** First Commission 1951**.
 
• The most current Finance Commission, chaired by** N. K. Singh,** a former member of the Planning Commission, was established in 2017.
 
• The Commission is appointed every five years, according to the Constitution, and consists of a chairperson and four additional members.

questions.question: What is the full form of UPSC?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Union Public Service Commission**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The full form of UPSC is **Union Public Service Commission**.
 
• UPSC is India's premier central recruiting agency responsible for appointments to and examinations for All India services and group A & group B of Central services.
 
• Established under **Article 315** of the Constitution of India, the UPSC conducts various exams such as the Civil Services Examination, Engineering Services Examination, and Combined Medical Services Examination, among others.
 
• The commission is mandated to ensure a fair and transparent recruitment process for the services under its purview.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **UPSC** was established on **1st October 1926** as the **Public Service Commission** but was later reconstituted as the **Federal Public Service Commission** by the **Government of India Act 1935**.
 
• **It was renamed as the Union Public Service Commission after independence**.
 
• UPSC is **headquartered **at **Dholpur House, New Delhi**.
 
• The commission is responsible for conducting exams for the recruitment of officers into the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Indian Foreign Service (IFS), Indian Police Service (IPS), and other central services.
 
• The chairman and other members of the UPSC are appointed by the President of India.
 
• The commission operates under the guidance of the** Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions**.
 
• UPSC ensures a merit-based selection process, thereby maintaining the integrity and efficiency of the civil services in India.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a constitutional body?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**NITI Aayog**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog** is NOT a constitutional body.
 
• NITI Aayog stands for **National Institution for Transforming India**, which was established by an executive resolution of the Government of India in 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
 
• Unlike the other options listed, NITI Aayog is a **policy think tank** of the Government of India and does not derive its authority from the Constitution.
 
• The **Election Commission, Finance Commission, and Union Public Service Commission** are all constitutional bodies, established under various articles of the Constitution of India.
 
• These constitutional bodies have specific roles and responsibilities defined by the Constitution to ensure the smooth functioning of the democratic framework and governance in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Election Commission of India** is established under Article 324 of the Constitution and is responsible for administering election processes in India.
 
• The **Finance Commission** is established under Article 280 of the Constitution and recommends the distribution of taxes between the Union and the States.
 
• The **Union Public Service Commission (UPSC)** is established under Article 315 of the Constitution and conducts examinations for recruitment to various civil services of the Government of India.
 
• **NITI Aayog** aims to foster cooperative federalism through structured support initiatives and mechanisms with the States on a continuous basis, recognizing that strong states make a strong nation.
 
• It provides relevant strategic and technical advice across the spectrum of key elements of policy to the central and state governments.

questions.question: How many other members are there in the Finance Commission EXCEPT, Chairman?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Finance Commission of India is composed of **five members in total**: one Chairman and four other members.
 
• The **Chairman** is selected based on their expertise in public affairs, whereas the other four members are chosen for their knowledge in finance, administration, and economics.
 
• The Finance Commission is a **constitutional body** established under Article 280 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The primary role of the Finance Commission is to **recommend the distribution of tax revenues** between the Centre and the States.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Constitutional Provisions**

 
 
• The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every five years under Article 280 of the Constitution.
 
• It is tasked with recommending measures to improve the financial health of the State and Union governments.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the Finance Commission**
 
 
• It determines the **division of net tax proceeds** between the Centre and States.
 
• It recommends the principles to distribute these funds among the states.
 
 
 
• **Qualifications of Members**
 
 
• The members of the Finance Commission must have specialized knowledge in finance, economics, public administration, or governance.
 
 
 
• **Recent Finance Commissions**
 
 
• The **15th Finance Commission**, chaired by N.K. Singh, was constituted in 2017 and submitted its final report for the period 2021-26.
 
• Its recommendations focus on **fiscal consolidation, tax devolution, and grants-in-aid** for the states.
